summary: Frontend only. (A) Meet him and the share video pass everything: on 4dxnbdm4 and dx22jcd8 the emo group has exactly 6 layers [blink, wink, blush, heart_eyes, kiss, shy] and there are no smile or brow_raise requests. The frames use ?v=7 (the real path is /assets/husbands/{slug}/{expr}.webp?v=7). The intro wink reaches >0.5 opacity 1.17-1.34s after the layers mount (1s delay plus the 300ms fade). Six taps gave wink, blush, heart_eyes, kiss, shy, wink. A second tap during each emotion was ignored (6/6). At most 1 [data-expr] layer was above 0.02, sampled every frame for about 22s with taps and autoplay. /card/4dxnbdm4?frames=0.95,2.2,4.2,5.9 reaches data-frames-ready=1, and a visual crop shows blink, wink, heart eyes, neutral. The reveal-video-button download works (tobias-woven-by-hand.mp4, 845KB). (B) The PageStack crossfade works but is not robust. I probed every frame on two full runs (1280x800 and 390x844) through Welcome->/strand/1->...->/strand/10->/bands->back->/strands/10->/bands->/weaving->/meet. Never more than 2 .page-cell. 1 cell once the leave finishes. On desktop the arriving medallion keeps its layout box: its top moves 89->101 only because of the scale(1.04->1) transform, and both panel items are centred in the same cell, so nothing is pushed or stacked. The phone CTA bar was never fully gone. Back works. Must-haves renders. Pre-weave medallions have data-woven=0, with 0 expression layers and no tap target, on strands 1/5/9, /bands and early /weaving. Meet has woven=1 and 6 layers. Run 1 failed 3 transition checks and run 2 failed 6. The cause is that the leaving cell is removed by a fixed 320ms setTimeout while its CSS fade can start late on a long first frame. When that happens the leaving screen (still at 0.72-1.0 opacity) disappears in one frame while the arriving one is at only 0.08-0.4. Desktop: s1->s2 (lowest 0.08), weaving->meet (0.08 and 0.15), bands->weaving (0.4). Phone: weaving->meet (0.99->0.49). (C) Reduced motion is broken: there is no 200ms fade (an instant cut), and the arriving content still sits 12px low for 150ms and then jumps.

ui_bugs.issue: The global rule `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important } }` (line 153) overrides the intended `.page-leave/.page-enter/.panel-* { animation: fade-* .2s }`. The computed animation-duration is 1e-05s, so screens hard-cut instead of fading over 200ms. Also, `.page-leave > main > *, .page-enter > main > * { animation: none }` loses on specificity to `.page-enter > main > :not(.fixed)`. So pg-in/pg-out still apply. The arriving content keeps the 0.15s delay with backwards fill at translateY(12px), then jumps up 12px (I measured matrix(...,0,12) for 150ms, then none). The leaving content jumps to -12px. .cta-enter keeps its .15s delay too.

The leaving cell is removed after a fixed LEAVE_MS=320ms setTimeout that starts at commit. Its CSS fade-out starts at first render. When mounting the next screen causes a long frame (Medallion, Meet card), the leave animation lags: it is still at opacity 0.72-1.0 when the timer removes it. The arriving cell is then only at 0.08-0.4, which gives a near-blank or pop frame. Seen intermittently in headless Chrome: desktop s1->s2 (lowest 0.08), weaving->meet (0.08 and 0.15), bands->weaving (0.4); phone weaving->meet (0.99->0.49). Most transitions are fine (lowest about 0.23-0.36).

action_items: Reduced motion: in the reduce block, use matching specificity: `.page-leave > main > :not(.fixed), .page-enter > main > :not(.fixed) { animation: none; }`. Then make the 200ms fades survive the global 0.01ms rule. Either add !important (`animation: fade-in .2s ease both !important` for .page-*, .panel-*, .cta-*), or exclude these classes from the global `*` rule. Drop the .15s delay on .cta-enter as well.

PageStack: remove the leaving cell on its own `animationend` (check e.target === e.currentTarget && e.animationName === 'fade-out'), with a safety timeout of about 700ms, instead of the fixed 320ms timer. Apply the same idea to useLinger (panel/building husband), so a late-starting animation is never cut off mid-fade.
Optional: to raise the lowest point of the crossfade (about 0.23-0.3 even on a good run), overlap more. For example, delay the leave fade or start the enter at about 80ms instead of 150ms.
critical_code_review_comments: face.js: emote('wink') on Meet and share-him-button does not advance st.i. So the first tap after the intro wink plays wink again, which is what the spec says. Note that the tap cycle and emote() share the s.cur guard, so a tap during the random autoplay mood is silently dropped (by design).
face.js comments still say 'nine frames' and 'eight expression frames'. There are now 7 frames and 6 layers. Stale comments in Meet.jsx line 61 and face.js lines 19 and 32.

StrandCTA: on phone, the leaving and entering bars both render pill buttons with the same data-testid inside different wrappers (strand-cta-bar-leaving and strand-cta-bar). During the 320ms window there are two [data-testid=weave-strand-button] elements. The leaving one has pointer-events:none, but tests or automation using .first could hit it.

Headless desktop frames are about 120-180ms apart at 1280x800, which makes the leave-timer race visible.
rca of the issue: Reduced motion: two CSS bugs. (1) Specificity: `.page-enter > main > :not(.fixed)` is (0,2,1), higher than `.page-enter > main > *` at (0,1,1), so the slide is never disabled. (2) The global `* { animation-duration: .01ms !important }` overrides the non-important `.2s` shorthand. Both are confirmed by getComputedStyle (fade-in/1e-05s, child pg-in/1e-05s/0.15s, transform 0,12 for 150ms). Pop: PageStack's useEffect timer (320ms) runs on wall-clock from commit. The CSS animation's start time is set when the first frame renders. A long frame (heavy mount) pushes the animation start later, so when the cell is removed its opacity is still high. I reproduced it in 2 of 2 full desktop runs, at different transitions.
